text:
maya: forwarding a customer escalation — they call our embeddings endpoint and get a 400 with 'invalid input shape'. quote from their client: "I only send a single string and it fails. Works in other SDKs tho?"

devin: can you paste the raw request body they sent? common culprit is passing a bare string vs. an array of strings. our embeddings endpoint expects "input": [..] for batching, some older SDKs accept a bare string but not our current API.

maya: here's what the customer pasted into support: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536",
  "input": "hello world"
}
```
They say their app used to work with another provider where single string was fine. Response: 400 {"error":"invalid input shape: expected array of strings or arrays"}

sophie: yup that's the mismatch. We validate top-level `input` to be an array. Recommend telling them to wrap in a list: "\"input\": [\"hello world\"]". Also watch out for accidentally double-nesting. I've seen `[["hello world"]]` from some clients which our decoder treats as batched arrays of token lists — causes shape parsing errors or dimension mismatches later. :warning:

maya: customer also reported a different error when they tried sending a precomputed vector (they were experimenting): 422 {"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: model expected 1536 got 1024"}. Any quick explanation?

devin: that one means they sent floats (embedding vector) instead of raw text. Our embeddings route accepts text and returns vectors; if someone uploads vectors expecting similarity-only behavior, they'll hit dimension checks. Model `open-embed-1536` expects 1536-length vectors. If they have vector length 1024, that's incompatible.

maya: customer confused because their client lib has two code paths — one that computes embeddings locally (older model) and another that calls our API. They accidentally sent the local vector to our API.

sophie: suggested repro steps to send to customer: 1) run curl with explicit array; 2) check response. Example: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["test string"]}'
```
If that works, problem is client-shape/encoding. Also ask them to `console.log(typeof input, JSON.stringify(input))` before sending.

maya: they tried the curl and it worked. They sent us their client's axios snippet, which had `data: JSON.stringify({model, input: sentences})` where `sentences` was coming from a library that sometimes returns a nested array when batching utility used `map` vs `flatMap`.

devin: so two concrete actions: 1) tell them to ensure `input` is a flat array of strings (or array of arrays of tokens if they have tokenized inputs, but only if model supports that) and 2) verify they are not sending vectors. We should also suggest adding a quick sanity check in their client: 
```
if (!Array.isArray(input)) input = [input];
if (Array.isArray(input) && input.length && Array.isArray(input[0]) && typeof input[0][0] === 'string') {
  // fine: array of strings
} else if (Array.isArray(input) && typeof input[0] === 'number') {
  throw new Error('Looks like you are sending a numeric embedding vector to the embeddings endpoint')
}
```

ops-bot: support_ticket#4392 updated: customer confirmed wrap-in-array fix works.

maya: one more ask — customer complained of high latency when they tried to batch 500 short strings in a single request. They saw timeouts. Advice?

devin: for throughput: batching helps but super-large batches can exceed server-side memory/seq limits and increase tail latency. Recommend batching ~64-256 strings depending on avg length. Also recommend enabling `streaming:false` for embeddings (it's not streaming) and using concurrent requests with a pool. If they need high throughput we should recommend Dedicated or rate-limit headers.

sophie: also remind them about Content-Encoding: gzip for big payloads. Some clients double-json-encode which inflates size and causes portal timeouts. For numeric-heavy payloads (vectors) that's different.

maya: closing summary posted to customer: 1) wrap single string in array, 2) flatten nested arrays, 3) don't send vectors to the embeddings endpoint, 4) if you need to send vectors use the similarity/vector route (if available) or use our embeddings-compare API, 5) for throughput use modest batch sizes or Dedicated capacity.

devin: addendum: I filed a small internal doc snippet we can paste into canned responses to avoid repeating. I'll add a note to the SDK team to ensure the JS SDK auto-wraps single strings into arrays and warns on numeric arrays.

maya: thanks — customer confirmed fix and asked us to keep the ticket open for one more day to monitor.

ops-bot: ticket 4392 -> status: awaiting monitoring (24h). :white_check_mark:
